findings.title: Arrival is counted only at consequence
findings.claim: The focus presents guidance as already arrived, yet the people treat arrival as incomplete until the earlier punitive pattern or punishment itself becomes present to them.
findings.mechanism: The two root_000009/B001 carriers name coming to the recipients, while root_001198/B002 supplies prior sequence and root_001198/B001 supplies frontal encounter. The independent relations in 39:54, 15:13, and 6:111 make those carriers meet a wider pattern of response before punishment, prior precedent, and face-to-face evidence, changing the waiting into a self-imposed threshold for recognition.
findings.reader_payoff: The exception is newly legible as delayed recognition rather than delayed guidance: what has come is present, but it is not counted until consequence can be faced.
findings.containment: The ordinary arrival of guidance and the possible arrival of punishment remain intact. This is a contextual resonance of the arrival and confrontation terms, not a claim that either form lexically means coercion or that all guidance is invalid without punishment.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication supplies the complete focus branch set; the independent connection targets provide exact Arabic and authored relations but do not supply target morphology or lexical analysis.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: Guidance has already reached them, but their refusal behaves as though arrival is unfinished until consequence reaches them too.
branch_activations.boundary: The contextual trigger does not redefine either أتى form as punishment or compulsion.

findings.title: The threshold is moved from guidance to consequence
findings.claim: The focus's already-arrived guidance is treated by the people as insufficient evidence until a decisive consequence arrives, so the blockage becomes a demand for coercive visibility.
findings.mechanism: The root_000009/B001 carriers are the completed arrival of guidance and the pending arrival of consequence. The independent 6:158 and 39:54 relations place belief before a decisive arrival and repentance before punishment, making contact with the focus's two arrival forms and changing the reading from missing information to a raised evidentiary threshold.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the verse names guidance as having come while still describing refusal: the refusal changes the standard for what will count as coming.
findings.containment: This retains the reader-walk's bounded threshold insight without importing its untyped wider examples as separate context claims. It does not say that the focus's arrival verbs themselves mean proof by force.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch and its two carriers are supplied, while the reader-walk source is legacy_unbound and the independent connection targets lack target morphology.

branch_activations.activation: These before/after relations contact the focus's arrival carriers and make the people's waiting a change in evidentiary standard rather than a lack of access to guidance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: They behave as though guidance has not truly arrived until a consequence is visible enough to compel recognition.
branch_activations.boundary: The threshold is an attributed contextual response, not a lexical definition of أتى or a claim that force is the only valid evidence.

findings.title: Prior precedent demanded as present confrontation
findings.claim: The earlier-peoples pattern is not merely remembered; the focus's final term lets it become something the people demand to encounter directly before they will accept guidance.
findings.mechanism: The qbl carrier supports both the prior-in-sequence facet and the frontal facet. The 15:13 relation supplies the established earlier-peoples pattern, while 6:111 supplies direct evidence that still fails to produce belief; together they make the contact between prior precedent and present confrontation explicit.
findings.reader_payoff: The closing alternatives become a portrait of mediated warning being rejected until the warning is turned into an encounter in front of the hearer.
findings.containment: The focus still names an ordinary precedent and punishment. The reader-walk's wider dispute framing is retained only as qualified contextual evidence; this does not claim that qbl always means both priorness and frontal encounter in every form.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk activation is anchored to the focus qbl occurrence and its nominated priorness branch; the cross-ayah relations have exact target Arabic but no target morphology.

findings.title: Forgiveness as protection before punishment
findings.claim: The focus's request for forgiveness can also be heard as an available protection from punishment, so waiting for punishment rejects an open protective relation rather than responding to an absent remedy.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier يَسْتَغْفِرُوا is the request-form occurrence of root_001096/B002. The exact 8:33 connection states that punishment is withheld while forgiveness is sought, and 71:10 supplies the same seeking-forgiveness action; these independent relations activate the branch's protection and request facets.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired blocked actions become one practical alternative: forgiveness is something the people could seek before the consequence they are waiting to see.
findings.containment: This is a cross-ayah contextual resonance, not a claim that forgiveness lexically means punishment or that 8:33 is a grammatical gloss of 18:55. The ordinary request for forgiveness remains recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The focus carrier and branch facets are supplied; the independent connection rows provide exact target Arabic and authored relations but omit target morphology and lexical analysis.

findings.title: The Lord as a restoring relation
findings.claim: The relational word for their Lord can carry a restoring and completing dimension beside its ordinary lordship, so seeking forgiveness becomes an appeal to an ongoing repair that the people leave unused.
findings.mechanism: The carrier رَبَّهُمْ is the focus's relational Lord expression. The wider 71:10 relation pairs the Lord with seeking forgiveness, while 11:117 places the Lord alongside a community's reforming condition; the adjacent focus forgiveness request supplies the independent contact that activates root_000532/B002's repair/completion facet.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgiveness is newly perceptible as a process of being restored, not only a legal request, while the warning's delay becomes refusal of that process before destruction.
findings.containment: This is a multi-step contextual resonance and does not displace the ordinary Lord/owner relation. It does not claim that every use of Rabb entails a developmental process or that reform guarantees reprieve in every setting.

epistemic.reason: The focus form and branch are supplied, but the restoration contact is multi-step and the connection targets supply exact Arabic without target morphology or lexical analysis.
